sentences.en: Hello, everybody, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your Twenties, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes and transitions of our 20s
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎回到《你二十岁的心理学》（The Psychology of Your Twenties），在这个播客里，我们探讨二十岁时面临的一些重大生活变化和转变，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及它们对我们心理的意义。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目中。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, it is so great to have you here back for another episode as we break down the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 新听众、老听众，无论你身处世界的哪个角落，非常高兴你能回来收听新的一期节目，和我们一起剖析二十岁的心理学。

sentences.en: The older we get, the less fun we have.
sentences.zh: 我们越老，收获的乐趣就越少。

sentences.en: That is how it seems to go, or that is the narrative that I think society would like to tell us.
sentences.zh: 事情似乎就是这样发展的，或者说这就是社会希望向我们灌输的叙事。

sentences.en: Our 20s are often presented as this, like, last decade for the kind of uninhibited joy and playfulness and recklessness
sentences.zh: 我们的二十岁通常被呈现为这样一种十年：充满了无拘无束的快乐、嬉戏和鲁莽，

sentences.en: that is very reminiscent of our childhood and our teen years.
sentences.zh: 这非常让人想起我们的童年和青少年时期。

sentences.en: But once we kind of start getting up there, all of that is apparently meant to stop.
sentences.zh: 但一旦我们开始步入成熟，这一切显然就都该停止了。

sentences.en: Our life revolves around work and commitments, financial and family obligations, and that kind of slice of the pie that is devoted to personal freedom and playfulness
sentences.zh: 我们的生活围绕着工作和承诺、经济与家庭义务打转，而那块留给个人自由和玩乐的蛋糕切片

sentences.en: is meant to get smaller and smaller.
sentences.zh: 注定变得越来越小。

sentences.en: Here's what I believe.
sentences.zh: 以下是我的看法。

sentences.en: I think that we, and the world in general, do not appreciate the value of play way into adulthood.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们以及整个世界，在很大程度上都低估了“玩耍”对成年生活的价值。

sentences.en: We do not really prioritize space in our life to be unproductively social, to just hang out and be silly, to be adventurous and imaginative,
sentences.zh: 我们并没有真正在生活中为无所事事的社交、闲逛和傻乐、冒险和想象留出空间，

sentences.en: because there is so much that takes up our focus.
sentences.zh: 因为有太多事情占据了我们的注意力。

sentences.en: And I think that is why a lot of us seem to feel like the older we get, the less joy there is in life.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是为什么我们很多人似乎觉得，人越老，生活中的快乐就越少。

sentences.en: We're losing this sense of wonder.
sentences.zh: 我们正在失去这种惊叹感。

sentences.en: We're losing out on something vital.
sentences.zh: 我们正在失去至关重要的东西。

sentences.en: Despite that, there are so many proven benefits of play.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，玩耍已经被证明有无数的好处。

sentences.en: Stronger relationships, better friendships, reduced stress, greater creativity, better overall happiness.
sentences.zh: 更牢固的关系、更好的友谊、减少压力、更强的创造力、更高的整体幸福感。

sentences.en: So today, I want to really present to you my argument for bringing back playdates for adults.
sentences.zh: 所以今天，我真的很想向大家提出我的论点：为成年人找回“约玩”（playdates）。

sentences.en: When we were kids and we would like have our parents call around to our friends' houses and, you know, schedule an afternoon together and the hours would, you know, swim past,
sentences.zh: 当我们还是个孩子的时候，我们会让父母给朋友家里打电话，你知道的，安排一个下午聚在一起，时光就会，你知道的，飞逝而过，

sentences.en: it was so delightful.
sentences.zh: 那真是太美妙了。

sentences.en: And it was so fun to just literally spend hours not doing much, but doing it with somebody else.
sentences.zh: 而且字面意思上花几个小时什么也不做，只是和另一个人在一起，真的非常有趣。

sentences.en: And we all know that's harder now.
sentences.zh: 我们都知道现在这更难做到了。

sentences.en: We don't hang out like we used to.
sentences.zh: 我们不像以前那样经常一起闲逛了。

sentences.en: There are a lot of factors to blame.
sentences.zh: 有很多因素可以归咎。

sentences.en: Technology is always the first culprit, but also just how busy we are, the time constraints and the societal beliefs about what it means to be an adult.
sentences.zh: 科技总是头号罪魁祸首，但还有我们的忙碌程度、时间限制以及社会对成年人含义的固有看法。

sentences.en: We are meant to be serious.
sentences.zh: 我们注定要严肃。

sentences.en: So we're meant to be mature.
sentences.zh: 所以我们注定要成熟。

sentences.en: And that kind of creates a lot of psychological restraints as well, like the fear of judgment or guilt and the conditioned behavior that comes along with that
sentences.zh: 这就产生了很多心理上的束缚，比如对评判的恐惧或内疚，以及随之而来的条件反射般行为，

sentences.en: to be more mature and responsible and professional.
sentences.zh: 即变得更加成熟、负责任和专业。

sentences.en: But today we are going to break down what psychology has to say about the value of play, how important it is to have unstructured moments where you just hang out with others,
sentences.zh: 但今天我们要剖析心理学对玩耍价值的看法，拥有那些你只是和他人闲逛的非结构化时刻是多么重要，

sentences.en: even when we feel silly about doing it, why we might be missing out and how we can actually bring back this spark and this energy into our lives.
sentences.zh: 甚至当我们对此感到有点幼稚时，为什么我们可能会错过这些，以及我们如何才能真正将这种火花和能量重新带回我们的生活。

sentences.en: We are also going to talk about concepts like parallel play, play personalities,
sentences.zh: 我们还将讨论诸如平行游戏、玩耍人格、

sentences.en: extroversion, introversion, ambiversion, and so much more.
sentences.zh: 外向、内向、中间性格等等概念。

sentences.en: I cannot tell you how excited I am for this episode.
sentences.zh: 我无法形容我对这一期节目有多么兴奋。

sentences.en: I feel like so many of us already know this to be true.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们中的很多人其实内心深处都知道这是真的。

sentences.en: We are craving more in-person opportunities for connection.
sentences.zh: 我们渴望更多的面对面社交机会。

sentences.en: We're craving more ways to really disconnect from reality for a little while and just like get back to that childhood wonder and awe and joy and enjoyment.
sentences.zh: 我们渴望有更多的方法真正从现实中抽离一会儿，就像回到童年的惊叹、敬畏、快乐和享受中去一样。

sentences.en: And hopefully this persuades you even more so, convinces you even more so, that this is something that you need to implement in your own life.
sentences.zh: 希望这能更进一步说服你、让你更加确信，这是你需要在自己的生活中落实的事情。

sentences.en: So without further ado, let's talk about what I believe are all the highly compelling reasons why we should be bringing back adult play dates.
sentences.zh: 那么废话不多说，让我们来谈谈我认为为什么我们应该找回成年人的“约玩”的所有极具说服力的理由。

sentences.en: As always, let's start super simple here.
sentences.zh: 像往常一样，我们从超级简单的地方开始。

sentences.en: Let's start from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 让我们从头说起。

sentences.en: Why do we actually need play?
sentences.zh: 我们为什么其实需要玩耍？

sentences.en: When we kind of think about our hierarchy of needs as human beings, things like food and water, safety, belonging, community, love, money, they all seem fairly obvious.
sentences.zh: 当我们思考人类的需求层次时，食物和水、安全、归属感、社群、爱、金钱这些东西，似乎都显而易见。

sentences.en: Play, less so.
sentences.zh: 玩耍则不然。

sentences.en: Especially as adults, play really falls off of our list of essentials, even our list of extras or luxuries.
sentences.zh: 特别作为成年人，玩耍真的从我们的必需品清单中滑落了，甚至连额外的或奢侈品清单都算不上。

sentences.en: For children, we understand it's a bit more valuable.
sentences.zh: 对于孩子，我们明白它的价值要高一些。

sentences.en: Play is actually quite essential to how children learn those fine and gross motor skills.
sentences.zh: 玩耍对于孩子学习精细和粗大运动技能其实相当重要。

sentences.en: They learn how to socialize and collaborate, develop their imagination and abstract thinking.
sentences.zh: 他们学习如何社交和合作，培养想象力和抽象思维。

sentences.en: You kind of get the picture.
sentences.zh: 你大概能想象得到了。

sentences.en: There were some really fascinating papers and articles written in the late 90s and early 2000s that suggested that play deprivation or play deficiency,
sentences.zh: 在90年代末和2000年初，有一些非常迷人的论文和文章指出，缺乏玩耍或玩耍不足，

sentences.en: children who were not allowed to play freely as children, perhaps grow up to have less empathy, more difficulty forming social bonds.
sentences.zh: 那些在童年时不被允许自由玩耍的孩子，长大后可能会缺乏同理心，在建立社会纽带方面有更多困难。

sentences.en: How did they discover this?
sentences.zh: 他们是如何发现这一点的？

sentences.en: They looked at mass shooters and people who were incarcerated and people who had done jail time and they compared their level of free play as children
sentences.zh: 他们研究了大规模枪击犯、服刑人员以及坐过牢的人，并将他们童年时期的自由玩耍水平与

sentences.en: to a separate sample of people who hadn't done jail time and what they found was one of the differences was this capacity to be playful and this capacity to be free as children.
sentences.zh: 另一组没有坐过牢的人进行对比，他们发现其中一个区别就在于这种作为孩子的游戏能力和自由能力。

sentences.en: Obviously, there were a ton of other factors associated with that as well, but the presence or absence of play and the quality of play, particularly in childhood development,
sentences.zh: 显然，这其中还关联着大量其他因素，但玩耍的存在与否以及玩耍的质量，特别是在儿童发展中，

sentences.en: does have proven long-term impacts on our emotional intelligence, our resilience, even things like brain size.
sentences.zh: 确实对我们的情商、韧性甚至大脑大小等都有已被证实的长期影响。

sentences.en: There is even more evidence showing us that parts of our brains that are most developed in those early years between like 18 months to eight years are the ones that respond best
sentences.zh: 甚至有更多证据表明，我们大脑中在18个月到8岁这些早期发育最完善的部分，正是那些对

sentences.en: to the kind of active experience induced by being playful.
sentences.zh: 由玩耍引发的这种活跃体验反应最好的部分。

sentences.en: It's all about the neural connections that play builds through problem solving and creating and imagining and also cooperating that makes it so valuable.
sentences.zh: 这一切都关乎玩耍通过解决问题、创造、想象以及合作所建立的神经连接，这正是它如此珍贵的原因。

sentences.en: But does that end when we turn 18?
sentences.zh: 但这会在我们满18岁时结束吗？

sentences.en: You know, have we done, has play kind of done all that it can for us?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们做完了吗，玩耍对我们所有的积极作用到头了吗？

sentences.en: Those neural systems are in place now.
sentences.zh: 这些神经系统现在已经就位了。

sentences.en: It's time to get serious.
sentences.zh: 是时候变得严肃了。

sentences.en: We don't need it anymore.
sentences.zh: 我们不再需要它了。

sentences.en: You know, it's done what it's good for.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它已经完成了它的使命。

sentences.en: Obviously, I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 显然，我不这么认为。

sentences.en: Absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 绝对没有。

sentences.en: Play is not just frivolous and it's not just for kids.
sentences.zh: 玩耍不仅仅是轻浮的，它也不仅仅属于儿童。

sentences.en: It's something that is an inherent part of our human nature, probably even our animal nature as well.
sentences.zh: 它是我们人类天性中固有的一部分，可能也是我们动物本能中固有的一部分。

sentences.en: It might seem like a waste of time or unproductive, but there was this really fascinating
sentences.zh: 它可能看起来像是浪费时间或没有生产力，但《纽约时报》曾有一篇非常精彩的文章是这样说的：

sentences.en: New York Times article that put it this way.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》曾有一篇非常精彩的文章是这样说的。

sentences.en: That is the whole point.
sentences.zh: 这正是重点所在。

sentences.en: That is the whole point of play is that it is silly and unproductive and a quote unquote waste of time.
sentences.zh: 玩耍的全部意义就在于它是愚蠢的、没有生产力的，并且是所谓的“浪费时间”。

sentences.en: Play is a way of deliberately bringing about joy without that joy being attached to some specific goal or requirement.
sentences.zh: 玩耍是一种故意带来快乐的方式，而这种快乐并不附带于任何特定的目标或要求。

sentences.en: It is just like fun for the sake of fun.
sentences.zh: 它就像是为了快乐而快乐。

sentences.en: Whereas so much about our adult lives is goal or outcome orientated.
sentences.zh: 而我们的成年生活有太多是目标或结果导向的。

sentences.en: You know, we ride our bikes because we want to lose weight.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们骑自行车是因为我们想减肥。

sentences.en: We go to Pilates class to get in shape.
sentences.zh: 我们去上普拉提课是为了塑形。

sentences.en: We do work trivia to maintain social connections.
sentences.zh: 我们参加工作聚餐是为了维持社交关系。

sentences.en: We cook simply to feed ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们做饭仅仅是为了喂饱自己。

sentences.en: Everything that perhaps used to bring us joy as children or even as teenagers becomes something that is part of a broader goal and kind of part of a broader structure and routine.
sentences.zh: 所有那些过去可能给我们带来快乐的事物——无论是作为孩子还是青少年——都变成了更广泛目标的一部分，并融入了更广泛的结构和常规之中。

sentences.en: But when we are doing things like playing Frisbee in the park or I don't know, mermaids in the pool or charades with our friends, even video games, we're kind of stepping back
sentences.zh: 但当我们做一些事情，比如在公园里玩飞盘，或者我不知道，在泳池里假装是人鱼，和朋友玩看图猜词，甚至是电子游戏时，我们其实是在从

sentences.en: from the structure of our daily lives.
sentences.zh: 日常生活的结构中抽身出来。

sentences.en: And it's within those daily lives that we often are kind of forced to follow a set of rules or forced to need to be taking something off of our to-do liSt.
sentences.zh: 正是在这些日常生活中，我们经常被迫遵循一套规则，或者觉得必须从我们的待办事项清单上划掉某些东西。

sentences.en: When we give ourselves those opportunities to take a step back, to enjoy the moment, to be silly, we're channeling this in a child version of us that still exists
sentences.zh: 当我们给自己这些机会退后一步、享受当下、傻乐时，我们正在唤醒内心那个依然存在的童年版本的自己，
